Knowledge of the operations of a wing, various Air Force Reserve entities, other MAJCOMs and Air Force, and their relationships in overall management and execution of military operations, evaluations, and missions. 3. Knowledge of tactical and strategic warfare, and wartime readiness posture; Skill in exercising tact and diplomacy in dealing various individuals when accomplishing duties. 6. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win ... Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. THIS IS AN AIR RESERVE TECHNICIAN OFFICER POSITION. This is an Air Reserve Technician (ART) Officer position located at 442 FIGHTER WG with the military rank of O-6/COL, AFSC: 091W0. For questions concerning military eligibility please contact the Air Force Reserve Qualification Center at 1-800-257-1212. MajorDuties: The primary purpose of this position is to serve as Air Reserve Technician (ART) officer to serve as the senior ART/Commander and as such, be responsible for planning, organizing, coordinating, directing, and controlling the fulltime activities and operations of the wing. As Commander of a Numbered Air Force (NAF), or Wing which is either a host organization or an organization tenanted on an Air Force installation of another command, plans, organizes, directs and controls the activities and operations of the unit through subordinate functional chief positions. Responsible for accomplishment of the variety of functions comprising the unit. Primary functions which characterize the unit commanded include aircraft maintenance, aircraft operations and training, and flying safety. At host locations a variety of base operating support functions, e.g., civil engineering, supply, personnel, resource plans, procurement, comptroller, etc., also comprise the reserve wing or group commanded. Directs through the subordinate supervisory structure, several hundred positions involved in accomplishment of the wide variety of functions essential to the fulfillment of the unit's mission.

Air Reserve units and members are subject to immediate call to active duty in mobilization to meet a national emergency. Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serve as Director of Strategy & Posture Division, Office of the Assistant Chief of Staff, G5, HQ IMCOM Europe. The G5 Strategy & Posture Division is responsible for the planning, coordination, and implementation of Installation Management Command Europe's (IMCOM-E) support to U.S. European Command (EUCOM), U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM), and U.S. Army Europe & Africa (USAREUR-AF).

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. Wiesbaden is without a doubt one of the most attractive cities in Germany. The capital city of Hessen is sometimes referred to as "Nice of the North" and rightfully so considering the many mansions, the historic Kurhaus, the casino and the State Theater. Wiesbaden is well known as a great spa city since ancient times. It has 27 hot, saline springs and its mild climate and park-like setting continue to make it a popular resort and conference center. Wiesbaden has an abundance of leisure activities, providing a cosmopolitan atmosphere blended with an attractive cultural ambiance, extraordinary architecture and marked by endearing charm. Located in a premier wine growing area on the Rhine River only 20 minutes from the Frankfurt International Airport. Efficient mass transportation systems are readily available. Visit the Wiesbaden Army Community website at: www.wiesbaden.army.mil for local garrison support and http://www.wiesbaden.de for city plans and attractions.
MajorDuties: Advise the IMCOM-E Director on posture and strategic stationing implications impacting the force posture strategies of operational forces in Europe.
Responsible for the overall responsibility for the analysis, development, and implementation of IMCOM-E Strategy and Force Posture programs in support of USAREUR-AF.

Plan, organize, and manage, through subordinate staff, the impacts on Garrison operations and master plans regarding force posture changes and stationing plans to include buildup of new force structures, capabilities and installations.
Coordinate the actions of the IMCOM-E Staff and subordinate units when identifying new methods of operations or re-engineering current operations.

Responsible for the development and implementation of polies affecting IMCOM-E force posture support, such as restructure, stationing and re-stationing, realignment and/or return to CONUS of Army forces in Europe and Africa.
Responsible for the direction and coordination of operations necessary to accomplish the assigned responsibilities of the department.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serves as the Senior Data Analysis Subject Matter Expert and Regional Supervision and Administration (S&A) Dashboard Manager. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Build Strong With Us at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), where engineering excellence meets public service. As the Nation's premier engineering, design, and construction management agency, we deliver innovative and efficient solutions that strengthen national security, support economic growth, and reduce disaster risks for communities across the country. At USACE, you will find meaningful work, collaborative teams, and opportunities to grow your career while making a lasting impact. We seek talented professionals with vision, creativity, leadership, and technical expertise to help solve some of the Nation's toughest engineering challenges. Build your purpose. Build your profession. Build your future. Discover why USACE is a great place to work and Build Strong With Us.
MajorDuties: Oversees the fiscal balance of the Supervision and Administration (S and A) program to ensure regional and district objectives are met.

Consolidates and prepares S and A reports based on template updates received from respective NAD District teams to identify performance variances between projected and actual placement, expenses and income.
Collects and analyzes statistical data to provide easy interpretation by management officials.
Directs project execution data operations and long-range strategic planning guidance across the Europe District's multi-mission portfolio.

Collaborates closely with supervisors, staff across various divisions, external agencies, contractors, and international host-nation entities to provide technical guidance, influence management to implement findings, and drive workforce improvements.

Utilizes a comprehensive understanding of federal regulations to integrate U.S. military standards with diverse host-nation requirements, international agreements, and Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA) constraints.
Advises on the potential benefits and uses of automation and technology to improve the efficiency of program operations.
Details.Evaluations: You will be evaluated based on how well you meet the qualifications listed in this vacancy announcement. Details.JobSummary: This is a Direct Hire Authority (DHA) solicitation utilizing the DHA for Certain Personnel of the DoD Workforceto recruit and appoint qualified candidates to positions in the competitive service. About the Position: This position serves as a Senior Program Analyst responsible for providing financial management advice to Life Cycle Project Managers and other program analysts regarding management of all fund types during design and construction program execution.
Details.SubAgencyName: USACE Europe District, Programs and Project Management Division
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Build Strong With Us at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), where engineering excellence meets public service. As the Nation's premier engineering, design, and construction management agency, we deliver innovative and efficient solutions that strengthen national security, support economic growth, and reduce disaster risks for communities across the country. At USACE, you will find meaningful work, collaborative teams, and opportunities to grow your career while making a lasting impact. We seek talented professionals with vision, creativity, leadership, and technical expertise to help solve some of the Nation's toughest engineering challenges. Build your purpose. Build your profession. Build your future. Discover why USACE is a great place to work and Build Strong With Us.
MajorDuties: Provide financial management advice to Lifecycle Project Managers, Program Managers and Program Analysts regarding the management of multiple fund types during the planning, design, and construction phases.

Oversee the financial stewardship of assigned project funding on a daily basis, analyzing and monitoring both individual projects and overall programs in assigned areas with regard to statutory constraints and local forecasts.
Review the financial status of all assigned programs and perform comparative analyses for the expeditious and efficient use of project funding.
Monitor current working estimates and allocated funds, including reimbursable programs, to ensure that adequate funding and authority levels for program execution are available.

Serve as the primary point of contact with the Resource Management (RM) office on financial matters for assigned programs and apprise RM of final close out of records and/or estimates for the revocation of single and multi-year funds.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.SubAgency: Air Force Life Cycle Management Center/DP
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-03, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-13 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience includes planning, organizing, and directing Center-level human resources, civilian, military, and manpower functions through subordinate supervisors. Experience also includes advising senior leadership and coordinating with headquarters to develop and implement integrated human resources policies. Experience in applying management principles to analyze operations, restructure organizations, optimize resources, and execute supervisory duties such as mentoring staff and recommending candidates. Experience also includes communicating strategic positions and building effective working relationships with senior leaders, General Officers, and Senior Executive Service members across installations. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Mastery of advanced management and organizational principles and practices along with a comprehensive knowledge of human resources functions, e.g., civilian personnel, military personnel, manpower, etc., to develop and implement integrated approaches and solutions to significant human resources concerns and issues. Knowledge of USAF, AFMC, and AFLCMC organizations, programs, missions, and functions to analyze and determine human resources plans, programs, and initiatives to support customers' current and future requirements. Knowledge of safety and security regulations, practices, and procedures. Ability to plan, organize, and direct the functions and mentor, motivate, and appraise the staff of the directorate through subordinate supervisors. Ability to analyze, plan, and adjust work operations of one or more organizational segments to meet program requirements and objectives within available resources. Ability to communicate, both orally and in writing, to achieve stated positions or to make an adequate case for a particular strategy which may or may not be readily accepted but is the best solution to achieve overall AFLCMC goals. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MajorDuties: Exercises supervisory personnel management responsibilities at least 25% of the time. Directs, coordinates, and oversees work through subordinate supervisors. Plans, organizes, and directs the Center-level activities for the Directorate, Personnel Division. Provides subordinate supervisors and staff with direction and advice regarding policies, procedures, and guidelines. Reviews and structures organization to optimize use of resources and maximize efficiency and effectiveness of the organization. Serves as a confidential advisor to the Center Commander, Vice-Commander, and Executive Director for matters related to human resources. Works directly with manpower, military personnel, and civilian personnel offices at HQ Air Force Material Command (AFMC) and HQ USAF levels to develop and implement human resources policies across the Center. Represents the Personnel Directorate with a variety of installation and functional area organizations. Establishes, develops, and maintains effective working relationships with all levels of management and human resources personnel, including General Officers and Senior Executive Service members, located at Wright Patterson AFB, other AFMC Centers, HQ AFMC, and Air Force. Advises staff regarding policies, procedures, and directives of higher level management or headquarters. With the director, selects or recommends candidates for subordinate positions, taking into consideration skills and qualifications, mission requirements, and EEO and diversity objectives.

Specialized experience is experience in analyzing Major Command programs and discerning fiscal programming changes across diverse mission areas using qualitative and quantitative methods. Experience also includes applying the Planning, Programming, and Budgeting System (PPBS) and standard budgetary practices to formulate, justify, and execute budgets from the base to OSD levels. Experience in documenting programming decisions, analyzing funding trends, and utilizing financial data systems like the Command Management System (CMS) and Program & Budget Enterprise System (PBES) to process information. Experience also includes guiding program development, communicating effectively, and negotiating complex, resource-intensive proposals with management. In-depth knowledge of the Planning, Programming and Budgeting System (PPBS). This knowledge should be current and run the gamut from the Base-level process through the Air Staff and OSD process. Ability to discern changes in fiscal programming across AFMC Mission Areas, functional, and numerous AFMC field installations, and knowledge of the relationship of the various Air Force entities involved in overall planning, programming, and budgeting to include knowledge of Program Elements and Element of Expense investment codes. Knowledge of commonly used budgetary methods, practices, procedures, regulations, policies, and processes to formulate, justify, and execute assigned budget in support of the mission, structure, goals, work processes, and programs of assigned organization(s). Skill with personal computer software packages to include proficiency with spreadsheets, database, presentation, graphics, and word processing. Ability to apply knowledge of computer applications to effectively run the Command Management System (CMS) and the Program & Budget Enterprise System (PBES). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-02, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-11 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is experience in planning, organizing, and directing critical contractual, financial, and technical aspects of major subsystems or equipment acquisition programs through all lifecycle phases in accordance with Department of War (DoD) and Air Force acquisition laws, policies, and organizational structures. This includes experience in leading multi-functional teams of functional specialists-including engineering, contracting, manufacturing, program control, configuration management, and logistics-to evaluate contractor proposals, monitor program progress against objectives, and resolve complex, unprecedented acquisition challenges. Experience also includes preparing, presenting, and defending staff studies to executive-level government officials and industry partners, translating complex technical concepts into clear, concise communications, and establishing collaborative relationships across organizational boundaries to ensure mission alignment.. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. OR COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: Combinations of successfully completed post-high school education and experience may be used to meet total qualification requirements. NOTE: You must submit a copy of your transcripts. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of laws, principles, policies, and practices of systems acquisition and program management. Knowledge of business, industrial management, contracting procedures, technical concepts, and production practices to evaluate contractor proposals and activities. Knowledge of the missions, roles, functions, organizational structures, and operation of the Department of Defense, Air Force, and other entities that govern, interface with, and/or influence the systems acquisition process. Ability to communicate both orally and in writing, clearly, concisely, and with technical accuracy. Ability to establish and maintain good relationships with individuals and groups within the office, as well as, outside the immediate work unit. Ability to plan, organize, lead, and manage critical aspects of research, development, production, and support of subsystems or equipment, and integrate, analyze, and manage a variety of acquisition functions and personnel in support of the process. MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionTitle: SUPERVISORY MANAGEMENT ANALYST - DIRECT HIRE AUTHORITY
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-02, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-11 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is experience in planning, organizing, and directing the operations of a Manpower Office, which includes exercising supervisory personnel management responsibilities to assign work, set organizational priorities, and evaluate performance. Expertise extends to applying advanced qualitative and quantitative methods, management engineering principles, and analytical techniques to conduct comprehensive studies on manpower requirements, organizational structure, workload, and program cost. Experience in advising commanders, directors, and senior staff on complex manpower and organization matters, including organizational realignment, mission changes, and resource assessment. Background includes communicating effectively both orally and in writing to deliver briefings, coordinate actions with high-level stakeholders, and resolve critical issues affecting program efficiency and organizational performance. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of manpower and organization principles, methods, processes, and analytical techniques used to assess manpower requirements, organizational structure, workload, and resources use. Knowledge of qualitative and quantitative methods used to apply management engineering principles, management analysis concepts, work measurement, program cost analysis, and resource assessment. Knowledge of the missions, functions, programs, and organizational relationships of serviced activities sufficient to conduct studies, assess manning and skill-level needs, and recommend supportable manpower and organization actions. Knowledge of manpower resource principles and techniques as they relate to organizational realignment, mission change, closure actions, outsourcing, privatization, insourcing, and related manpower studies when applicable. Knowledge of safety and security requirements, practices, and procedures applicable to the work environment. Skill in applying analytical and evaluative techniques to identify, assess, and resolve issues affecting program efficiency, effectiveness, cost, workload, manpower requirements, and organizational performance. Skill in planning, organizing, and directing comprehensive manpower and organization analyses involving diverse organizations, functions, missions, and work processes. Skill in advising commanders, directors, supervisors, and staff on manpower and organization matters and developing recommendations that are clear, supportable, and mission-focused. Ability to plan, organize, and direct the work of a small to medium-sized organization, including assigning work, setting priorities, evaluating performance, developing employees, and improving work processes. Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, to prepare reports, present briefings, explain complex manpower issues, and coordinate actions with customers and stakeholders. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-02, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-11 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is experience in planning, coordinating, and executing military protocol activities and distinguished visits for senior executive leadership ("Top Five"), including changes of command, promotions, retirements, and executive-level conferences. This includes researching visitor backgrounds and applying comprehensive knowledge of DAF, AFMC, and civilian protocol courtesies, ranks, and precedence to prevent breaches of custom. Experience also includes managing event budgets to project and document expenditures, developing integrated execution plans under tight deadlines, and communicating persuasively both verbally and in writing to diverse internal and external stakeholders to achieve mission goals. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Comprehensive knowledge of WPAFB and its tenant organizational structure, functions, policies, and operations, etc., to ensure programs planned for visitors to WPAFB are accurate, comprehensive, informative, and are conducted within acceptable parameters in accordance with 88th ABW and AFMC policies. Comprehensive knowledge of organizational components, including the function/location/organizational structure and activities of other AFMC units, major commands, DAF, tri-service's executive and legislative liaison offices to determine types of programs appropriate for presentation to visitors from those organizations and the level of protocol courtesies to be accorded them based on rank, precedence, and significance to the mission. Comprehensive knowledge of proper civilian and military protocol courtesies to be accorded to visitors from both the United States and foreign governments that contributes to the ability to research special protocols and visiting requirements of foreign and U.S. dignitaries (etiquette manuals and guides, DAF/AFMC policies, regulations and procedures). Working knowledge of pertinent budgeting and accounting practices to project, monitor and document collections and expenditures. Ability to communicate both verbally and in writing, to achieve stated positions, or to make an adequate case for a particular strategy which may or may not be readily accepted but is the best solution to achieve overall mission goals. Ability to develop, analyze, evaluate and integrate plans and other documents related to assigned functions. Able to plan individual workload to meet deadlines. IDEAL CANDIDATE: We are seeking a candidate with a strong Protocol background: either 12+ months at the MAJCOM level or 24+ months at the Wing/NAF level. Furthermore, successful completion of the USAF Protocol Fundamentals Course and other recognized Protocol professional development curricula is highly desirable. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-02, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-11 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is experience in determining long-range functional manning requirements, analyzing workload surveys and specialized skill needs for evolving missions, and applying evaluative techniques to measure and improve organizational productivity and operational processes. Experience also includes utilizing systems such as the AFLCMC Resource Management Information System (RMIS) for strategic workforce planning, implementing integrated civilian and military human resource solutions, recommending policy improvements, and communicating workforce strategies to align with Directorate and AFLCMC goals. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of analytical and evaluative methods and techniques to apply to issues or studies concerning the efficiency and effectiveness of Directorate and other supported offices operations. Knowledge of the mission, major issues, program goals and objectives, work processes, and operations of the Directorate and other supported offices and Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC). Knowledge of management and organizational principles and practices along with a knowledge of human resource functions. e.g., civilian personnel, military personnel, and manpower, to develop and implement integrated approaches and solutions to significant human resource concerns and issues. Skilled in adapting analytical techniques and evaluation criteria to the measurement and improvement of program effectiveness and/or organizational productivity. Ability to communicate, both orally and in writing, to achieve stated positions or to make an adequate case for a particular strategy which may or may not be readily accepted, but is the best solution to achieve overall Directorate, other supported offices, and AFLCMC goals. Ability to utilize the AFLCMC Resource Management Information System (RMIS) to develop and utilize various reports in the analysis of human resource information necessary for strategic workforce planning. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-03, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-13 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is experience in serving as the subject matter expert to executive leadership in planning, organizing, and directing the integration activities of the Strategy, Planning and Programming Process (SP3). This includes utilizing expert knowledge of capabilities-focused planning, Air Force policies, and program goals to define, validate, and execute capability integration and process improvement plans. Experience also includes establishing continuous liaison with HQ AFMC, Air Staff, and DoD offices to integrate SP3 processes, and applying advanced organizational, qualitative, and quantitative analytical methods to measure program effectiveness. Additionally, experience in demonstrating leadership abilities to advise senior officials on complex, mission-oriented issues, leading significant changes in business practices, and preparing and presenting high-level, strategic briefings to influence key decisions. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. OR COMBINING EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: Combinations of successfully completed post-high school education and experience may be used to meet total qualification requirements KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Expert knowledge of effects-based, capabilities-focused planning, and Department of Air Force policy, procedures, and schedules for developing AF process improvement plans in support of AF and command goals and objectives, and methods of defining, developing, documenting, validating, gaining approval, and managing capability integration and mission assignment strategy execution and process improvement plans and strategies. Extensive knowledge of Air Force program goals and objectives, the sequence and timing of key operations events and milestones, and methods of evaluating the effectiveness of planning actions as related to actual events. Skill in reviewing processes and conducting extensive analysis of processes to substantiate change to organizational dynamics. Demonstrated leadership and managerial abilities, in conjunction with the authority to serve as a technical expert and consultant to AFMC leadership and other AF officials on extremely complex and highly diverse directorate mission-oriented issues to include capability integration and mission assignment activities. Mastery of advanced management, organizational, and analytical principles, methods techniques, and practices in conjunction with a comprehensive knowledge of the missions, roles, functions, organizational structures, and operations of AFMC, USAF, DoD, other agencies, and private industry, that govern, interface with, and/or influence the Strategic Plans, Programs and Assessments Directorate's missions and programs. Comprehensive knowledge of qualitative and quantitative techniques for gathering, analyzing and measuring the effectiveness, efficiency, and productivity of acquisition program and support activities, in addition to the ability to gather and analyze complex program information, make sound judgments concerning substantive program processes, procedures, and practices. Ability and professional stature to lead the development of significant changes in business practices and influence complex policy decisions. Demonstrated communication skills and abilities, verbal and nonverbal, in conjunction with the ability to present and influence decisions by the high levels of management, both within and outside of the directorate, and to support and defend recommendations to those levels. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-09, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes: (1) Working with administrative analysis and problem-solving techniques to evaluate staff processes, interpret administrative data, and develop recommendations to improve the efficiency of executive support operations; (2) Working with administrative structures, staff roles, and command channels of the Organization and higher-echelon Air Force/DoD organizations to effectively coordinate executive taskings and provide administrative advisory services; and (3) Working with advanced executive support systems and software (e.g., MS Office Suite, SharePoint, Defense Travel System) to manage complex scheduling, coordinate executive travel, generate data-driven reports, and facilitate high-visibility logistics. OR EDUCATION: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a Ph.D. degree or LL.M which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, if related. NOTE: You must submit a copy of your transcripts. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. NOTE: You must submit a copy of transcripts FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-09 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-11 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of administrative analysis and problem-solving techniques to evaluate staff processes, interpret administrative data, and develop recommendations to improve the efficiency of Wing executive support operations. Knowledge of the administrative structures, staff roles, and command channels of the Wing and higher-echelon Air Force/DoD organizations to effectively coordinate executive taskings and provide administrative advisory services. Knowledge of administrative rules and skill in using executive support systems (e.g., MS Office, SharePoint, DTS) to manage complex scheduling, executive travel, and high-visibility logistics. Skill in written and verbal communication to prepare clear, concise, and accurate reports, briefings, and correspondence for senior leaders and external stakeholders. Skill in planning and managing short and long-term projects and initiatives, including the ability to identify resources, track milestones, and resolve program shortfalls. Ability to exercise independent judgment and use tact and diplomacy to build successful cross-functional teams and resolve complex problems impacting the command mission. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Benefits of joining U.S. Army Garrison Yuma, Yuma, AZ, include ride share opportunities; on-post surplus housing; and access to Morale, Welfare & Recreation services like child-care and youth activities for school-aged children, food and beverage facilities, fitness center, pool, and discount military theme park tickets. For those living on-post there is an on-post elementary school for grades kindergarten thru 5th grade. Benefits of being an Army Professional include unique training and professional development opportunities, DoD and Federal Leadership Development programs, paid federal holidays, sick leave and annual leave accrued per pay period based on time in service, retirement benefits, 401K matching contributions, work life enrichment such Employee Assistance Programs, and the Army Civilian Fitness and Health Promotion Program. YPG is located near the Arizona-California-Mexico border, approximately 15 miles north of the outskirts of the city of Yuma (pop 87,000), Arizona. Yuma is a 2.5-hour drive from San Diego, CA and Phoenix, AZ, along Interstate Highway 8, and a 5-6 hour drive from Las Vegas, NV, in the heart of the great Sonoran desert where the US Army tests medium and long range artillery, aircraft target acquisition equipment and armament, armored and wheeled vehicles, and a variety of munitions, and personnel and supply parachute systems to ensure that America's ground forces have the equipment necessary to win our nation's battles.
MajorDuties: Assists in the development and implementation of effective marketing plans that support organizational goals, increase customer awareness, and drive program participation.
Contributes to comprehensive publicity, promotional, sales, and merchandising strategies tailored to target audiences and local market conditions.
Helps coordinate integrated marketing campaigns across print, digital, broadcast, and on-site channels to ensure consistent messaging and branding.
Provides recommendations on media layouts, advertising copy, photography, graphic design, print materials, and broadcast releases to improve campaign effectiveness.
Reviews marketing results and customer feedback to identify opportunities for improvement and support future planning efforts.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Details.Benefits: Working for Army Non-Appropriated Funds (NAF) can offer numerous advantages. Army NAF employment can provide a sense of pride and fulfillment, as you'll be supporting communities comprised of military and civilian personnel, and their families, which contributes to the Department of Defense's overall mission. We offer a wide range of career opportunities, including jobs in childcare, recreation, hospitality, and more. Many employees have opportunities for professional development, including training, education, and certification programs to help towards career advancement. As an Army NAF employee, you'll have access to some on-base facilities, including fitness centers, libraries, and many other amenities. Regular full-time and part-time employees are eligible for enrollment in health and life insurance, participation in 401k and retirement plans, and paid personal time off and federal holidays. NAF flexible employees, working in the United States or a U.S. citizen or spouse or child of a U.S. citizen working for a NAFI in a foreign area, are eligible to participate in the NAF 401(k) plan. Some flexible employees may also be eligible to receive health insurance. For a slideshow presentation regarding these benefits, please click the Review Our Benefits link below.
Details.OtherInformation: Area of Consideration The Area of Consideration for this vacancy announcement is Worldwide. (Military Spouse Preference (MSP) and Involuntarily Separated Military Preference (ISMP) eligible candidates are included in the area of consideration.) Manual Application Option If you are unable to apply online, you can complete a paper application. To get started, contact servicing NAF Human Resources representative or office listed in the Agency Contact Information section (at the bottom of this announcement) to request a copy of the application form. Be sure to submit your completed application form, along with your resume and any required supporting documents, no later than 1500 MST on 10/13/2026 to ensure timely processing. Important: Incomplete applications, including missing responses to questionnaire items may result in an ineligible rating. PCS Costs Payment of Permanent Change of Station (PCS) costs are not authorized based on a determination that a PCS move is not in the Government's interest. Allowances and Differentials This job is part of a pay-banded system. Sunday premium pay for regularly scheduled employees and night differential pay may be authorized by the Garrison Commander. Non-foreign overseas allowances, cost of living (COLA), and differentials will not be paid, contingent upon eligibility. Important Information Regarding Access to Certain Federal Facilities: Access to certain federal facilities may require a REAL ID-compliant driver's license/ID (marked with a star) or an Enhanced Driver's License (EDL) from WA, MI, MN, NY, or VT. See https://www.tsa.gov/real-id for details. Your Application may be Considered for Multiple Opportunities: After you apply, your application remains valid for 90 days and may be referred to hiring officials as new vacancies arise. Additional referrals may occur for up to 90 days after the closing date. Termination of Spouse Employment Preference Refusal of a military spouse to participate in established recruitment procedures for a Regular Full-Time (RFT) or Regular Part-Time (RPT) position (for example, interview, and so forth) is considered a declination of employment and is a basis for termination of Spouse Employment Preference (SEP) entitlement for the current Permanent Change of Station (PCS) of the sponsor.
